narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **10% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this might sound low, it’s still high enough to require extra support—like taking remedial courses—to help you stay on track. Think of it like a warning light on a dashboard: it’s not saying disaster is certain, but it’s telling you to pay attention and take action before things get harder.

The biggest reason behind this prediction is your **number of past class failures**. Unlike most students, who haven’t failed any classes before, this small but meaningful setback is a red flag. It suggests that, while you’ve worked hard, there may be gaps in your understanding that need addressing now to avoid bigger challenges later.

Another key factor is **why you chose this school**. Most students pick their school because of the course or its proximity to home, but your decision was driven by its reputation. While reputation is great, it doesn’t always mean the school’s structure perfectly matches your needs—especially if you’re still figuring out how to balance your workload. This might mean you’re putting extra pressure on yourself to meet high expectations, which can be tough if you’re not getting the right support.

Finally, your **father’s level of education** plays a role. Compared to students whose fathers have higher education, those with secondary-level education (like yours) have historically faced slightly more academic hurdles. This isn’t about blame—it’s about recognizing that some students need a little more guidance to overcome these trends.

The good news? Remedial courses are designed to fill those gaps. They’ll help you catch up on any missed concepts, adjust to the school’s expectations, and build confidence before your final exams. Focus on attending these sessions, ask questions when you’re unsure, and use this as a chance to strengthen your study habits. You’ve got this—this is just a nudge to make sure you’re fully prepared.
